record.question: Caseating necrosis, a type of necrosis characterized by a cheese-like appearance, is strongly associated with granulomas caused by which type of pathogen?
record.explanation: Answer C: Mycobacteria. Caseating granulomas are classically and strongly associated with mycobacterial infection, especially tuberculosis. Other infections can produce granulomas, so this is the strongest offered association rather than an exclusive rule. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK344406/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430935/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
